CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
1. Region means Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government means the Government of Manggarai Regency.
3. Regent means the Regent of Manggarai.
4. The administration of the protection of women and children means the process, method, and act of administering protection for women and children.
5. Woman means a human being of the female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child means a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence means any form of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering—physical, emotional/psychological, economic, sexual, and social—toward the victim.
8. Violence against women means any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion, or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children means any form of action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
10. Victim means a woman, including female workers, and a child who experience misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly, as a result of such violence.
11. Protection of women means all acts aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, the prosecution service, the courts, social institutions, and other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child protection means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service means an action taken as soon as possible for the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Community means individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are to: a. prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children; b. assist women and children victims of violence in the legal process both litigation and non-litigation in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
c. provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence; and
d. restore the physical and psychological condition of women and children victims of violence.

Article 5
Letter a What is meant by protection and assistance is that every victim has the right to receive protection at the local level (regional) due to their status as a member of the local community, national protection due to their status as a citizen or resident, and international protection due to their status as a human being, a member of the world community (Human Rights).
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.

Letter g Integrated services are services that include medical services (related to physical and psychological or mental injuries), legal services (related to a person's rights, obligations and responsibilities) and psychosocial services (related to rights, obligations and responsibilities associated with social matters, and other socio-economic needs) as well as spiritual services.

Article 9
(1) Regional apparatus that carries out the function of empowerment and protection of women and children conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures and implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of institutions/work units that implement policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 10
(1) Evaluation of the implementation and policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 6
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. providing education on anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. collecting data and information on Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention, handling, recovery and rehabilitation efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the duties of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 13
In the event that the Integrated Service Center has not yet been established based on this Regional Regulation as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1), then the duties and obligations of the Integrated Service Center shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs the function of empowerment and protection of women and children.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 8
(1) Regional Government in the implementation of protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

I. GENERAL
Efforts to implement protection for women and children must continue to be carried out and the implementation should be conducted in a coordinated and integrated manner among related agencies and/or bodies. To support the smooth implementation of the protection for women and children in Manggarai Regency, a regional regulation is needed that regulates the protection of women and children.
In order to support such implementation, it is necessary to regulate the mechanism and cooperation starting from the recovery of victims in terms of their physical and/or psychological condition, by determining the duties and functions of each party and the obligations and responsibilities of health workers, spiritual counselors and volunteer companions. To make integrated services more effective, this regional regulation establishes a mechanism that will coordinate among service officers, while simultaneously formulating program plans for improving efforts to implement protection for women and children.
Cooperation in implementing protection for women and children is directed at prevention, handling and restoration of the victims' condition to their original state both physically and psychologically within a not too lengthy period of time, so that victims can carry out their daily activities and can live in the community as before. Therefore, services must be implemented as maximally as possible immediately after there is a complaint or report from victims to obtain services for the recovery of the condition of women and children victims of violence. In addition, efforts to eliminate violence preventively are also continuously carried out in various ways, so that violence against women and children in the long term can be eliminated or at minimum its numbers can be reduced.

Because understanding or interpretation of religious principles differs individually while the nature of the principles (static norms) cannot change, there should be proper understanding so as not to have negative impacts because some applications can be adjusted and some others are dogmatic, while situational indicates that the implementation of gender equality cannot be applied the same to all strata of society. Therefore vandana shiva calls it equility in diversity (equality in diversity).
Gender is a social construction that distinguishes between the roles of men and women based on space and time that continuously changes.
Letter b Non-discrimination means not making distinctions for any reason and in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Best interests of the victim, means that in all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Pasal 4 explicitly lists “eksploitasi” and “perdagangan perempuan dan anak” (trafficking of women and children) as forms of violence, and the elucidation defines “eksploitasi” generally (forcing women/children to do something without regard to their development). However, the text does not specifically mention “eksploitasi seksual” (sexual exploitation) or “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery). “Kekerasan seksual” is listed separately, but that is not the same as sexual exploitation/slavery. Since the retrieved English passages accurately reflect this (general exploitation + sexual violence + trafficking, but no explicit sexual slavery/sexual exploitation), the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the actual policy text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be over-inclusive for this specific indicator.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
1. Region means Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government means the Government of Manggarai Regency.
3. Regent means the Regent of Manggarai.
4. The administration of the protection of women and children means the process, method, and act of administering protection for women and children.
5. Woman means a human being of the female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child means a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence means any form of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering—physical, emotional/psychological, economic, sexual, and social—toward the victim.
8. Violence against women means any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion, or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children means any form of action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
10. Victim means a woman, including female workers, and a child who experience misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly, as a result of such violence.
11. Protection of women means all acts aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, the prosecution service, the courts, social institutions, and other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child protection means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service means an action taken as soon as possible for the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Community means individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are to: a. prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children; b. assist women and children victims of violence in the legal process both litigation and non-litigation in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
c. provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence; and
d. restore the physical and psychological condition of women and children victims of violence.

Article 10
(1) Evaluation of the implementation and policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9
(1) Regional apparatus that carries out the function of empowerment and protection of women and children conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures and implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of institutions/work units that implement policies, programs, activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER X
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 13
In the event that the Integrated Service Center has not yet been established based on this Regional Regulation as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1), then the duties and obligations of the Integrated Service Center shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs the function of empowerment and protection of women and children.

CHAPTER IX
FUNDING
Article 12
Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other legitimate and non-binding sources of financing.

Article 11
(1) The Integrated Service Center is obligated to report in writing the implementation of protection services for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.
(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) The submission of the report as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 2
Letter a Equality and gender justice is a condition where the portion of the social cycle of women and men is equal, harmonious, balanced and in harmony. This condition can be realized if there is fair treatment between women and men. The implementation of equality and gender justice must pay attention to contextual and situational issues, not based on mathematical calculations and not universal in nature. This view distinguishes at least 3 contexts of a person's life in family, society and religion. Contextual example from a religious perspective: recognizing inheritance rights. Because understanding or interpretation of religious principles differs individually while the nature of the principles (static norms) cannot change, there should be proper understanding so as not to have negative impacts because some applications can be adjusted and some others are dogmatic, while situational indicates that the implementation of gender equality cannot be applied the same to all strata of society. Therefore vandana shiva calls it equility in diversity (equality in diversity).
Gender is a social construction that distinguishes between the roles of men and women based on space and time that continuously changes.
Letter b Non-discrimination means not making distinctions for any reason and in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF MANGGARAI REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2018
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Efforts to implement protection for women and children must continue to be carried out and the implementation should be conducted in a coordinated and integrated manner among related agencies and/or bodies. To support the smooth implementation of the protection for women and children in Manggarai Regency, a regional regulation is needed that regulates the protection of women and children.
In order to support such implementation, it is necessary to regulate the mechanism and cooperation starting from the recovery of victims in terms of their physical and/or psychological condition, by determining the duties and functions of each party and the obligations and responsibilities of health workers, spiritual counselors and volunteer companions. To make integrated services more effective, this regional regulation establishes a mechanism that will coordinate among service officers, while simultaneously formulating program plans for improving efforts to implement protection for women and children.
Cooperation in implementing protection for women and children is directed at prevention, handling and restoration of the victims' condition to their original state both physically and psychologically within a not too lengthy period of time, so that victims can carry out their daily activities and can live in the community as before. Therefore, services must be implemented as maximally as possible immediately after there is a complaint or report from victims to obtain services for the recovery of the condition of women and children victims of violence. In addition, efforts to eliminate violence preventively are also continuously carried out in various ways, so that violence against women and children in the long term can be eliminated or at minimum its numbers can be reduced.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 6
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. providing education on anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. collecting data and information on Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention, handling, recovery and rehabilitation efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the duties of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

REGENT OF MANGGARAI
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 8
(1) Regional Government in the implementation of protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

6.3.rationale: The Indonesian definition of “Korban” in Pasal 1 angka 10 explicitly includes “perempuan termasuk Tenaga Kerja Perempuan” (women including female workers). The retrieved English candidate passage [6.3-3] contains the same: “Victim means a woman, including female workers…”. If the indicator is simply whether the policy recognizes/includes women workers as a relevant group (intersectional mention), this is sufficient to answer ‘Yes’. The judge incorrectly required additional ‘special measures’ targeted to women workers, which is a stricter criterion than what the text-and-indicator pairing suggests. Therefore the main issue is the judge’s reasoning, not retrieval or translation.
